 Judgment

Petitioners being parents of the deceased Niharika M., filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the insurer and owners of Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 alleging that on 26.02.2024 at 10.00 a.m., when Niharika and her mother - petitioner No.2 are standing beside Dodda Aladamara - Tavarekere Main road, near Harshaganavi Kalyanamantapa within the limits of Tavarekere P.S., driver of Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 drove the same negligently from Tavarekere side, dashed the same to Niharika, thereby caused accident,
caused grievous injuries to Niharika.

Immediately after the accident, Niharika has been shifted to People Tree Hospital, wherein first aid has been provided, then shifted to NIMHANS Hospital,
Bengaluru, however, at NIMHANS hospital Niharika succumbed to the injuries.
2. As on the date of accident, Niharika was aged about 6 years.
3. Regarding the accident, Tavarekere police registered a case in Crime No.55/2024.

4. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 Insurance Company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denied the allegation regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident, age and status of Niharika.
5. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.2 and 3 owners of Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 remained absent.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 04.02.2025, this Authority has framed the following issues:

sentences.text:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 26.02.2024 at about 10.00 a.m., near Harsha Ganavi Kalyana Mantapa, on Dodda Alada Mara - Tavarekere Main road,
within the limits of Tavarekere police station, in view of the negligent use of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-51- D-1978, Car dashed to Niharika, D/o Murthappa, resulting in the injuries to Niharika, who succumbed to those injuries on the way of NIMHANS?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

7. On 04.01.2025, 04.03.2025 petitioner No.1 - Murthappa deposed as P.W.1 and produced 13 documents at Exs. P.1 to P.13.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative; Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.18,76,433/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation from the respondents.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- In the evidence P.W.1 stated that on 26.02.2024 at 10.00 a.m., when Niharika and her mother - petitioner No.2 are standing on the side of Dodda Aladamara - Tavarekere Main road,
near Harshaganavi Kalyanamantapa in order to cross the road, driver of Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 drove the same negligently from Tavarekere side, dashed the same to Niharika,
thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Niharika.
11.

P.W.1 further stated that, immediately after the accident, public have shifted Niharika to People Tree Hospital, wherein first aid has been provided, then shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein Niharika succumbed to those injuries.
12.
In the written statement respondent No.1 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident.
13. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 submitted that he never witnessed the accident.

14. Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR and complaint pertaining to Crime No.55/2024 registered by Tavarekere police against driver of Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 for having committed the offence punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and Section 187 of IMV Act, on the basis of the complaint presented by petitioner No.2 - Kala.

Ex.P.2 is the copy of report dated 04.03.2024 Murthappa vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105231384/
3 submitted by HC-385 of Tavarekere P.S. to PSI by producing the Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 which has caused accident.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the copy of Car seizure mahazar.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of sketch of place of accident.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of Motor Vehicle Accident Report.
Ex.P.8 is the copy of statement of petitioner No.2 Kalavathi recorded on 04.03.2024 about identification of car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 which caused accident.
Ex.P.9 is the copy of Medico Legal Case opinion dated 26.02.2024 forwarded by People Tree Hospital to Police Inspector, Tavarekere P.S.
Ex.P.10 is the copy of Inquest Mahazar.
Ex.P.11 is the copy of P.M.Report.

Ex.P.12 is the copy of Charge Sheet filed by Tavarekere police in Cr.No.55/2024 against Renuka Prasad, S/o.Nagaraju, driver of the Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 for having committed the offence punishable under Sections 279 and 304(A) of IPC and Section 187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.13 is the copy of Birth Certificate of Niharika, daughter of petitioners.
15. In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioners regarding reason, mode and consequences of the accident.

16. Hence, I have concluded that, on 26.02.2024 at 10.00 a.m., when Niharika and petitioner No.2 are standing beside Dodda Aladamara - Tavarekere Main road, near Harshaganavi Kalyanamantapa within the limits of Tavarekere police station, Renuka Prasad, S/o.Nagaraju negligently drove the Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 from Tavarekere side, dashed the same to Niharika, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Niharika, who succumbed to those injuries at NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

In the evidence affidavit, P.W.1 - Murthappa S/o.Venkateshappa, father of Niharika stated that as on the date of incident, his daughter Niharika was hale and healthy, very active and brilliant student.
In the petition petitioners stated that as on the date of accident, Niharika was aged about 6 years.
In the P.M.Report and Inquest Mahazar, age of Niharika is noted as 5 years.
In the birth certificate marked at Ex.P.13 date of birth of Niharika, daughter of petitioners is noted as 13.08.2019.
Hence, it is clear that as on the date of incident, Niharika was aged about 5 years 6 months.

18. The copy of the Judgment dated 12.09.2024 passed in Miscellaneous First Appeal No.11440/2011 C/w. Miscellaneous First Appeal No.206/2018 (Lakshminarayanappa @ Moogappa and others Vs. M/s.Royal Sundaram Allianz Ins. Co. Ltd. & Another), which has been produced by the petitioners in MVC No.3806/2024, reveals that, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka pleased to award compensation worth of Rs.18,76,433/- to the parents of the deceased who was less than 15 years and also insurer of the vehicle which was the reason for accident is bound to provide medical insurance in the name of claimants to the extent of Rs.10,00,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Judgment passed in MFA No.11440/2011 referred above, is directly applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case.
In this case deceased Niharika was aged about 5 years 6 months as on the date of incident and petitioners being the parents of Niharika are claiming compensation.

19. As referred above, in MVC No.3806/2024 on the basis of Judgment dated 12.09.2024 passed in MFA No.11440/2011 C/w MFA No.206/2018 recited by the petitioners, this authority awarded compensation of Rs.18,76,433/- to the petitioners.

Therefore, in this case also, it is fit and proper to Murthappa vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105231384/
4 award compensation worth of Rs.18,76,433/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation to the petitioners who are the parents of the deceased Niharika and also entitle for medical insurance to the extent of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondent No.1 insurer of Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978, which caused accident and to that effect award is to be passed.

sentences.text: Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly.
20. Issue No.3:
In the written statement, respondent No.1 - Insurance Company admitted the subsistence of policy with respect to Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 as on the date of incident.

In the reply dated 04.03.2024 submitted to the Investigating Officer to the notice issued under Section 133 of the IMV Act, respondent No.2 - Venkatesh S/o.Dasappa noted that during accident, Renuka Prasad was driving the Car bearing No.KA-51-D- 1978.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident, the respondent No.2 and 3 have violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the insurer and owners of the Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, I answer Issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.18,76,433/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs Seventy Six Thousand Four Hundred and thirty three only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.1, being the Insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.

The respondent No.1 being the Insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-51-D-1978 shall issue medical insurance in the name of the claimants to an extent of Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees Ten Lakhs only) as per Judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, dated 12.09.2024 passed in MFA No.11440/2011.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally.
After deposit of compensation, 50% of the compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioners by crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.

The surplus compensation amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioners in any of the bank till petitioners attain the age of 50 years without permitting to create any encumbrance, however, reserving liberty to withdraw periodical interest once in 3 months in accordance with law.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
